 L.E.A.D. Academy teacher arrested after allegedly selling pills to student, court documents say 
 A former teacher at L.E.A.D. Academy is now behind bars, accused of selling drugs to a child. By WSFA 12 News Staff Published : Oct. 22, 2026 at 5:09 PM CDT | Updated : 22 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google MONTGOMERY, Ala. ( WSFA ) - Court documents have revealed more details about the arrest of a teacher at a charter school in Montgomery.
 Langston Carter, 30, was taken into custody Thursday after Montgomery police were called to L.E.A.D. Academy on the Eastern Boulevard.
 Court records say a student was found in possession of two 5 mg oxycodone hydrochloride pills and 325 mg of acetaminophen pills. The student told officers he got the pills from Carter, his teacher.
 Former L.E.A.D. Academy teacher Langston Carter, 30, is facing multiple charges after he was arrested on Oct. 22, 2026, according to court records. (Source: Montgomery County Detention Facility) The student said he paid $10 for the pills after Carter allegedly offered to sell them to him on multiple occasions. He was told to CashApp the money to Carter’s girlfriend, but he had to ask a fellow student to send the money because he didn’t have a CashApp account. Court filings indicate the transaction was later verified by investigators.
 After the money was sent, the student got the pills from Carter in the classroom, according to court documents.
 L.E.A.D. Academy confirmed Thursday that students were placed on lockdown that afternoon at the direction of the Montgomery Police Department “to ensure integrity of the investigation.”
 Court filings say after hearing the accusations from the student, a K-9 officer conducted an open-air sniff outside of Carter’s vehicle. The K-9 indicated there was an odor, and police opened the trunk where they reportedly found a “sling style bag” with the following items inside:
 6.9 grams of marijuana 
 A digital scale 
 Empty plastic bags 
 18.9 grams of mushroom-infused gummies 
 Nineteen 5 mg oxycodone hydrochloride pills 
 325 mg of acetaminophen pills 
 A Beretta 9mm loaded handgun 
 Other narcotic-related items 
 In a statement posted Friday morning , the school confirmed the teacher, now identified in court records as Carter, has been fired.
 Montgomery police say Carter is facing multiple felony charges including:
 Possession of a firearm on school property 
 Two counts of unlawful distribution of a controlled substance 
 First-degree possession of marijuana 
 He is currently being held in the Montgomery County Detention Facility on a $300,000 bond.
